standard_prerequisites.name: In a local ring an element whose complement from a relation involving two generators lies in the maximal ideal forces one of the two coefficients to be a unit
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the comparability of divisibility from the principality of the ideal generated by two elements.

standard_prerequisites.name: Two distinct maximal ideals can be separated by elements lying in each but not the other, and such elements are mutually nondivisible
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that comparability of divisibility forces the ring to be local.

standard_prerequisites.name: If every two elements are comparable by divisibility then every finitely generated ideal is principal by induction, and a valuation ring is an example
standard_prerequisites.use: Completes the cycle of equivalences and handles the final statement.

core_obligations: Assume the second condition and let two elements be given: write the ideal they generate as principal, and if the generator vanishes both elements are zero; otherwise write the generator as a combination of the two and each element as a multiple of the generator, display the resulting relation, and use locality to deduce that one of the two multipliers is a unit, so that one element divides the other (proof lines 37651-37661).

Assume comparability of divisibility and show that the ring is local: two distinct maximal ideals give elements each lying in one and not the other, which are mutually nondivisible, a contradiction (proof lines 37663-37669).
Still assuming comparability, deduce by induction that every finitely generated ideal is principal, which gives the second condition (proof lines 37669-37670).

Record that the equivalence with the linear ordering of ideals is straightforward and that the final statement about valuation rings follows from the standard result characterizing them (proof lines 37670-37672).
proof_roadmap: From principality of finitely generated ideals and locality, derive comparability of divisibility (proof lines 37651-37661).
From comparability, derive locality and principality by the mutual nondivisibility of separating elements and by induction (proof lines 37663-37670).
Record the equivalence with the linear ordering of ideals and the valuation ring case (proof lines 37670-37672).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes nonzero rings in which any two elements are comparable by divisibility by two further conditions: every finitely generated ideal is principal and the ring is local, and the ideals are linearly ordered by inclusion (statement lines 37637-37649). The proof runs a cycle with explicit computations: from principality and locality, the relation obtained by writing the generator of an ideal as a combination of two elements and each element as a multiple of the generator forces one multiplier to be a unit; conversely, comparability forces locality because separating elements of two maximal ideals are mutually nondivisible, and induction gives principality of finitely generated ideals, while the equivalence with the linear order on ideals and the case of valuation rings are recorded as straightforward (proof lines 37651-37672). The two explicit algebraic steps are what make the cycle work. The counted statement contains the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed.
